description.summary: compositor-side visuals and animations

protocol.description:
Lets a client hand a surface (a layer-shell surface or one of its subsurfaces) to the compositor as a "visual" whose offset and opacity the compositor can animate on its own clock. While an animation runs the client does not need to commit or redraw: the compositor re-composites the already submitted buffers every frame. This is the DirectComposition-style split: clients provide content once, the compositor owns motion. See Ether docs/GPU_COMPOSITION_PLAN.md (G3).
Version 2 adds inset clipping (ether_visual_v1.set_clip / animate_clip). Version 3 adds parent-coordinate rectangle clipping (ether_visual_v1.set_clip_rect / unset_clip) and compositor-driven scrolling (ether_scroller_v1): the compositor follows touchpad fingers, runs inertia and wheel animations on its own clock and samples them at each frame's target presentation time, so scrolling never waits for the client. See Ether tools/dispatch/tasks/fp4-compositor-scroll.md.

description.summary: creates visuals for surfaces

request.name: get_visual

description.summary: create a visual for a surface

request.description: At most one visual may exist per surface; a second get_visual for the same surface raises the visual_exists error.

entry.name: visual_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a visual

entry.name: scroller_exists
entry.summary: the visual already has a scroller

request.name: get_scroller

description.summary: create a compositor-driven scroller for a visual

request.description: The visual's surface is the content surface: a subsurface whose buffer holds the realized part of the scrollable content. The compositor positions it (through the visual offset) from the scroll position it samples every frame. At most one scroller may exist per visual.

interface.name: ether_visual_v1

description.summary: compositor-animated offset, opacity and clip of a surface subtree

interface.description: All requests are double-buffered and applied on the next wl_surface.commit of the associated surface (following subsurface synchronization rules). Offset and opacity are purely visual: input hit-testing keeps using the surface's real position. Offsets are in surface-local logical coordinates and accumulate down the subsurface tree; opacities multiply down the tree.

description.summary: drop the visual; the surface returns to offset 0 and opacity 1
set the visual offset immediately (cancels a running animation)
set the opacity immediately (cancels a running animation)

request.name: animate

description.summary: animate offset and opacity from their presented values

request.description: Starts from the currently presented offset and opacity (so a new animate continues smoothly from wherever a previous one was interrupted; the interrupted one receives the cancelled event). Timing starts at the first frame in which the commit is applied, plus delay_ms. Progress follows the cubic Bezier (x1, y1, x2, y2) over duration_ms.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: client-chosen id echoed in done / cancelled

request.name: set_clip

description.summary: set the clip insets immediately (cancels a running clip animation)

request.description: The clip rectangle is the surface's own extent (its logical wl_surface size, placed where the surface is presented, i.e. including the visual offset) shrunk by the four insets. It clips this surface and its whole subsurface subtree; nested clips intersect. Insets are logical, measured inward from each edge; negative values are treated as 0, and insets that meet or cross leave nothing visible. The initial value is 0, 0, 0, 0 (no clipping). Like offset and opacity the clip is purely visual: input hit-testing is unaffected. Clip and offset/opacity are independent channels: set_clip and animate_clip never cancel an offset/opacity animation, and set_offset, set_opacity and animate never cancel a clip animation.

request.name: animate_clip

description.summary: animate the clip insets from their presented values

request.description: Same timing rules as animate (starts from the presented insets, timing begins at the first frame in which the commit is applied plus delay_ms, cubic Bezier progress over duration_ms; an interrupted clip animation receives the cancelled event). done and cancelled are shared with animate, so the client should keep serials distinct across both channels. Typical use: reveal a backdrop from its top edge while its content stays fixed on screen (animate top from the surface height to 0).

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: client-chosen id echoed in done / cancelled

request.name: set_clip_rect

description.summary: clip the visual subtree to a rectangle in parent coordinates

request.description: The rectangle is in the parent surface's local logical coordinates and does not move with this visual's own offset. Double-buffered. This channel is independent of the version 2 inset clip: when both are set on the same visual they are intersected.

description.summary: remove the parent-coordinate clip rectangle (double-buffered)
the animation (animate or animate_clip) with this serial reached its end values
the animation (animate or animate_clip) with this serial was replaced or cancelled

interface.name: ether_scroller_v1

description.summary: compositor-driven scrolling of a content surface

interface.description: All requests except scroll_by / scroll_to are double-buffered and applied atomically on the next commit of the content surface. The viewport is both the clip of the content and the scroll input area: while the pointer is inside the innermost viewport, axis events on the scroller's axes go to the compositor's tracker and are not forwarded to the client (except while Ctrl is held). Pointer hit-testing itself is unchanged: the content surface has an empty input region and pointer events land on the parent surface; the client maps viewport coordinates to content coordinates with the last offset event.

description.summary: drop the scroller; the content surface keeps its last offset

entry.name: bad_realized
entry.summary: realized size does not match the buffer

description.summary: viewport rectangle in parent surface logical coordinates
full content size; scrollable range is [0, extent - viewport]
scrollable axes mask: 1 = vertical, 2 = horizontal, 3 = both

request.name: set_realized

description.summary: content-coordinate rectangle held by the current buffer

request.description: The logical buffer size of the content surface must equal width x height when the commit is applied, otherwise the bad_realized error is raised.

description.summary: fill color for viewport areas not covered by the realized content
animate by a delta (keyboard, page keys); applied immediately
scroll to a position, animated or immediate; applied immediately

event.name: offset

description.summary: scroll position sampled for an output frame

event.description: Sent at most once per output frame, before that frame is submitted: the position that will be shown, and the frame's target presentation time (CLOCK_MONOTONIC).

description.summary: phase change; serial echoes a finished scroll_by / scroll_to (else 0)
